EXEC.examples.output-trap.title: The OUTPUT parameter trap
EXEC.examples.output-trap.sql:
CREATE PROCEDURE #Lib_GetCopyCount @Branch varchar(10), @CopyCount int OUTPUT
AS
    SELECT @CopyCount = 3;   -- Sample value; would query Cat_BookCopy in practice
GO
DECLARE @n int = -1;
EXEC #Lib_GetCopyCount @Branch = 'A01', @CopyCount = @n;         -- Missing OUTPUT
SELECT @n AS Missed;    -- Result: -1, value never came back (caller must mark OUTPUT too)
EXEC #Lib_GetCopyCount @Branch = 'A01', @CopyCount = @n OUTPUT;  -- Correct
SELECT @n AS Correct;   -- Result: 3
GO

AS

GO
EXEC #Lib_RawNames
    WITH RESULT SETS ((Branch varchar(10), CopyCount int));  -- Renames Col1/Col2
GO

RETURNS TABLE
AS
RETURN
    SELECT v.CopyNo, v.LoanDays

    WHERE v.LoanDays <= @Days;   -- Like a view with parameters; the optimizer inlines it

CREATE FUNCTION.examples.multi-statement.title: Multi-statement table-valued function
CREATE FUNCTION.examples.multi-statement.sql:
CREATE OR ALTER FUNCTION dbo.Lib_Numbers (@Max int)
RETURNS @Result TABLE (n int PRIMARY KEY)
AS
BEGIN
    DECLARE @i int = 1;
    WHILE @i <= @Max
    BEGIN
        INSERT INTO @Result VALUES (@i);   -- Only its own table variable can change
        SET @i += 1;
    END
    RETURN;
END
GO
SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total FROM dbo.Lib_Numbers(5);   -- Result: 5
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS dbo.Lib_Numbers;
